newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates end sharply up on tight funds.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates end sharply up on tight funds.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended sharply higher on Tuesday amid tightening liquidity at the peak of routine monthly payroll demand and an auction of state bank shares, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 7.784 percent against Monday's 7.499 finish, well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper jumped to 8.00 percent from 7.25-7.50.
Dealers said the government's five-day auction of some 418 million shares in Chiao Tung Bank, which began on Monday, was expected to siphon some T$30 billion in liquidity out of the banking system.
State firms' handover of T$60 billion in revenues to the state treasury beginning this month has further squeezed liquidity, dealers said.

Government bond yields closed higher, reflecting a modest annual rise in the July consumer price index, which was announced on Tuesday, and the central bank's decision last week to raise two key interest rates, dealers said.
The consumer price index was up 3.3 percent in July compared to July 1996, though officials said Taiwan remained on track to keep inflation tamed at about two percent for all of 1997.
The benchmark 86/4 bond yield was at 6.16 percent against 6.1375.
